status_rule: A check may be VALIDATED only after an Unreal Editor or playable-build verification.

checks.pass_condition: All titles, nodes, dossier text and reconstruction prompts remain readable without overlap.
Layout scales cleanly and visual density remains balanced.
No undersized text, excessive empty space or broken material scaling.
Graph drag is smooth, predictable and never drags the dossier panel.
Mouse-wheel zoom keeps the pointed graph area stable and usable at min/max zoom.
Node selection is immediate and the selected state is unmistakable.
Opening enters Game+UI input and closing reliably restores game-only input.
Dossier title, category, state, reliability and description are readable at all target resolutions.
Category accents are distinguishable without relying on color alone for critical meaning.
Contradictions are immediately recognizable as broken/conflicting connections.
Unknown nodes remain enticing but do not reveal hidden title/description content.
The Sarei branch can progress from first trace through evidence discovery to reconstruction.
At least one reconstruction succeeds through an alternate evidence path.
The reconstruction explains its historical cause before/with the gameplay unlock.
Node states, sources, reconstructions and unlock values survive save/load roundtrip.
Opening cue is audible but restrained and does not mask dialogue.
Repeated selection remains comfortable and non-fatiguing.
Contradiction cue signals tension without reading as an error buzzer.
Reconstruction cue feels like convergence/understanding, not loot or level-up.
Archive animation, particles and links do not introduce visible hitching on target hardware.
Optional Niagara/material FX justify their cost; remove any effect that adds cost without clear visual value.
The screen reads as solemn, archival, ash-bound and memory-driven rather than generic fantasy UI.
No code, asset or gameplay dependency requires LITD 1/Godot systems.
Every imported final asset is LITD_ORIGINAL_REUSABLE or documented LICENSED_REUSABLE.
